item.title: Jury convicts a man of first-degree murder for the 1996 killing of rap icon Tupac Shakur
item.description: A jury found Duane "Keffe D" Davis guilty of orchestrating the 1996 killing of rap icon Tupac Shakur, finally bringing a measure of resolution to a case that had gripped hip-hop fans for decades.
item.content:encoded:
A jury found Duane "Keffe D" Davis guilty of orchestrating the 1996 killing of rap icon Tupac Shakur, finally bringing a measure of resolution to a case that had gripped hip-hop fans for decades.

(Image credit: Bizuayehu Tesfaye)

item.title: Army Secretary Dan Driscoll is stepping down, White House says
item.description: Army Secretary Dan Driscoll is stepping down after 18 months on the job, the White House said Monday, in the latest departure of a top military leader during the Trump administration.
item.content:encoded:

item.title: Nearly 200 witnesses to Charlie Kirk shooting apply for victims' benefits in Utah
item.description: While the high-profile shooting at Utah Valley University had only one homicide victim, Kirk's assassination was witnessed by thousands in person and even more as video spread online.

item.title: Trump officials cut political interference ban after unusual Census Bureau report
item.description: After the Census Bureau issued a report tied to a Trump-aligned think tank, the bureau's parent agency cut language banning political interference from its scientific integrity policy, NPR learned.

item.title: Jurors deliberate in the trial of rap icon Tupac Shakur's killing
item.description: Jurors said Duane Davis is guilty of murder in orchestrating the killing of Tupac Shakur. The rap star was gunned down in a gang-related drive-by shooting in Las Vegas in 1996.

item.title: Paperwork, lines, hours on hold: There's a 'Time Tax' on Americans who need help most
item.description: Annie Lowrey explores the administrative burdens people face applying for government benefits. It's not just about wasted time: "When the government treats us like this, we don't trust it," she says.

item.title: At least 15 people missing after Grand Canyon flash flood
item.description: Several people are missing or unaccounted for after severe flash flooding in the Grand Canyon on Saturday caused significant damage.

item.title: The U.S.-Venezuela oil deal won't lower your gas prices. Here's what you need to know
item.description: The Trump administration announced a deal Friday to develop a vast amount of Venezuela's oil reserves, with the U.S. taking a majority stake. Energy experts say there are many reasons to be skeptical.
